method_as_stated: MAIN SIMULATIONS ARE NOT HOOMD. The paper states the grand canonical Monte Carlo was done with the authors' own C++ code. Two dimensions, periodic box of 53.3 x 53.3 particle diameters. The pair potential is the experimentally validated DNA-hybridisation potential of Rogers and Crocker (2011), its width rescaled to about 5% of the particle diameter. Species A-A never bind (E_AA = 0); E_AB and E_BB are the well depths. Initial state: particles at random at 0.5% area fraction, equal to the ideal-gas reservoir density; the two species have equal reservoir chemical potentials. Moves: displacement, insertion/deletion and species flip, accepted by the Metropolis rule, with insertion/deletion and flips attempted on average once per 1,000 displacements. Each run is at least 2e10 displacement trials. Order parameter Phi = (2/pi) arctan(Psi6/Psi4): above about 0.9 is hexagonal, below about 0.5 square. Free-energy landscapes in crystal size N_c and Phi by umbrella sampling with WHAM; 200 unbiased runs launched from saddle points follow the landscape. Hydrodynamics is absent from every simulation. HOOMD-BLUE APPEARS ONLY as the engine cited for a preliminary molecular-dynamics check that also shows the checkerboard-to-stripe transition; their set-up is in the Supplementary Information, which is not in this file, so no HOOMD version, integrator, time step or run length is stated in what was read. EXPERIMENT: 619-nm polystyrene spheres grafted with DNA by strain-promoted click chemistry, particle A carrying strand S and particle B a mixture of S and its complement S*, the mixing ratio alpha being the fraction of S on B; suspension at about 1.0% volume fraction and about 1:1 A:B, squeezed between two plasma-cleaned coverslips; temperature by a thermoelectric stage under PID control; quench to just above the melting temperature and hold about an hour; bright-field video on a Nikon Eclipse Ti2 with a CoolSNAP HQ2 camera, confocal images on a Leica SP8.
